tools.change: WRONG FOR THE UK AS BUILT. The tool averages four frequencies (0.5, 1, 2, 4 kHz) and grades with the American six-step scale (normal to 25 dB, mild, moderate, moderately severe, severe, profound above 90). The British Society of Audiology averages FIVE frequencies (250, 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 Hz) and has FOUR descriptors: mild 21 to 40, moderate 41 to 70, severe 71 to 95, profound in excess of 95 dB HL. Examples of what a UK clinician would be shown wrongly: 22 dB reads "within normal limits" (British: mild); 60 dB reads "moderately severe", a grade the British scale does not have; 92 dB reads "profound" (British: severe). The asymmetry flag (15 dB between the two averages) is also not the UK rule: NICE NG98 uses 15 dB or more at any 2 adjacent test frequencies. Change: a fifth field (250 Hz), the British descriptors, and the NICE asymmetry rule or no asymmetry flag. The audiologist role should see it too. SECOND PASS. Both British sources were read again and confirm the first pass figure for figure. British Society of Audiology (August 2018, marked for review in 2023, no newer version on the page): the average of FIVE frequencies; mild 21 to 40, moderate 41 to 70, severe 71 to 95, profound in excess of 95 dB HL; it defines no "normal"; a frequency with no response counts as 130 dB; each ear by itself; the descriptors are not to be the sole ground for providing hearing support. NICE NG98, 1.3.2: "consider" an MRI when the asymmetry is 15 dB or more at any 2 adjacent test frequencies (0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz); NICE gives no grades and no average. TWO EXAMPLES RUN ON THE CODE. (1) Thresholds of 15, 20, 25 and 40 dB, and 10 dB at 250 Hz: the screen shows 25.0 dB, "Within normal limits (up to 25 dB)"; the British five-frequency average is 22 dB, mild hearing loss. (2) Right ear 20, 20, 40, 40 dB and left ear 20, 20, 20, 25 dB: the averages are 30 and 21.3, so the tool raises no flag; at 2 and 4 kHz the ears differ by 20 and 15 dB, which meets the NICE rule. The tool cannot apply that rule at all: it is given only the other ear's average.

tools.change: DIFFERENT FROM THE UK CHARTS. The tool uses the simple rule (add or subtract 13 cm, halve) and a range of 8.5 cm either side. The RCPCH UK-WHO charts read the mid-parental centile from a comparator and give the target height range as "±7 cm" (four children out of five); RCPCH's digital charts average the parents' height z-scores with a regression factor and say this is more accurate "particularly where there's a large difference between parents" (Wright and Cheetham 1999). The UK chart was read again (the boys' 2 to 18 chart): four boys out of five reach an adult height within ±7 cm of the mid-parental target, and the chart adds that the height predicted from the child's own centile (within 6 cm) is usually closer to the final height than the mid-parental target. The college's digital-charts page describes its more accurate method (the parents' height z-scores averaged, with a regression factor) and lists mid-parental height among calculations not yet offered by its programming interface. EXAMPLE: mother 160 cm, father 180 cm, a boy: the screen shows 176.5 cm and a range of 168.0 to 185.0 cm; with the chart's range it is 169.5 to 183.5 cm. tools.change: Keep it off until rebuilt on NICE NG203. Three things. (1) Units and limits: NICE states the albumin-to-creatinine categories in mg/mmol (less than 3; 3 to 30; over 30); the kit classifies in mg/g after conversion, so values just above 3 or 30 mg/mmol fall one category low (the pack already says this). (2) THE REFERRAL FLAGS ARE NOT NICE'S. The code flags "refer" at GFR below 30, at category A3, and at a fall of more than 25% in a year. NICE NG203 refers on: a 5-year risk above 5% on the 4-variable Kidney Failure Risk Equation; an ACR of 70 mg/mmol or more; an ACR above 30 with haematuria; a sustained fall of 25% or more WITH a change of category within 12 months; a sustained fall of 15 ml/min/1.73 m2 or more per year; and four more. The labels say "KDIGO criterion"; a UK doctor follows NICE. (3) Who sees it: in the UK chronic kidney disease is found and followed in general practice, so this is a core tool, not an internal-medicine tool. NICE also asks laboratories for the CKD-EPI creatinine equation and prints no ethnicity adjustment. SECOND PASS. NICE NG203 was read again, in full, as a PDF, and confirms the first pass figure for figure: A1 below 3, A2 3 to 30, A3 over 30 mg/mmol; a first result between 3 and 70 is confirmed on an early-morning sample; the eight referral criteria; the CKD-EPI creatinine equation. EXAMPLES RUN ON THE CODE (it converts mg/mmol to mg/g and cuts at 30 and 300): 3.0 mg/mmol is called A1 (NICE: A2) and 31 mg/mmol is called A2 (NICE: A3); an ACR of 35 mg/mmol with no blood in the urine is flagged for referral as "A3" (by NICE it is not: above 30 needs haematuria, or the figure must reach 70); a GFR that falls from 44 to 32 in a year is flagged (by NICE it is neither a change of category nor a fall of 15). kitMechanismsMissing: A country cannot change WHO SEES a tool. The roles of each tool are written once in the shared English set (countries/_dil/en/araclar/arac1-3.ts); a country can only switch a tool off (kapali), rename units (birimAdlari) or change words (degisen). The UK needs, for example, the vertigo note for general practice and neurology too.

A country cannot ADD a tool of its own. The list of role tools (EN_ROL_ARACLARI) and the one base tool (EN_TEMEL_ARACLAR) are shared by all five English-speaking packs. NEWS2, the acuity record or the UK concussion stages would appear in the United States pack as well.

A country cannot give a tool its NUMBERS. The kit leaves thresholds and intervals to the pack (parametreler), but the English set builds every tool without them (araciBicimle returns no parametreler), so none of the eight "mechanism ready" slots can be switched on for one country.
Country numbers are not converted to the unit the arithmetic uses. A limit for haemoglobin supplied in g/L would be compared with a value the kit has already turned into g/dL (anemi-izlem).
HbA1c has no unit in the kit (lab-izlem accepts 3 to 20 only): a value in mmol/mol is refused. It needs to be a laboratory quantity with a unit, like creatinine.

Limits in the kit that the UK states differently and cannot override: the albuminuria categories (mg/g, not mg/mmol), the hearing-loss grades and the four frequencies, the 8.5 cm range of the expected height, the BI-RADS categories of the report outline, the stage list of return to sport, the ASA class list.

"Base" means every role, allied professions included. There is no way to say "every DOCTOR role": a core clinical tool given as base would also show to the physiotherapist, the dietitian and the audiologist.

The role list is one shared set of 40 keys (lib/ulke/rolEslemesi.test.ts refuses any other key). A country can rename a role but cannot add one (geriatric medicine), drop one (the second dermatology) or split one (oncology into medical and clinical).
The features "my templates" and "consultations" are not switched on in any English-speaking pack, so their two base tiles do not exist here.

niceTerms.commercialReuseInsideUK: Allowed, free of charge, under the NICE UK Open Content Licence (clauses 2 and 4): UK-only, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive, commercial and non-commercial, including in one's own product or app. Conditions (clauses 5, 6, 10): recommendations, quality statements and substantial algorithms unchanged in wording and structure; nothing beside advertising or promotional text; attribution in NICE's form of words with a disclaimer; no endorsement implied; a breach ends the licence. Excluded: the BNF and its derivatives, Clinical Knowledge Summaries, full guidelines of the collaborating centres, economic models, logos. Third-party material inside NICE content needs its owner's permission (terms and conditions 18.4).
niceTerms.reuseOutsideUK: Not covered by the open licence. Terms and conditions 18.2: apart from personal study, no use, reproduction, translation or distribution outside the UK without NICE's prior written agreement; requests are subject to a fee and a licensing agreement, including for a product offered in other territories alongside the UK.
niceTerms.artificialIntelligence: Outside the open licence in the UK and abroad. NICE content cannot be used for AI purposes without written permission supported by a signed licence agreement, applied for on a form. Terms and conditions 18.3: every request, without exception, goes through an approval process, a licensing arrangement and a fee ("Reusing our content" mentions a fee only for international use: the pages disagree). The BNF, BNF for Children and Clinical Knowledge Summaries need their publishers' express permission for AI purposes. No page read defines "AI purposes".
niceTerms.forALawyer: Whether a plain calculator showing a NICE threshold, inside a product that also has an AI assistant, counts as an AI purpose is not answered by any page read. Anything given to a model does. Contact given on the licence page: reuseofcontent@nice.org.uk.
